reconstructed_theorem_text: Let X be an arbitrary type equipped with a measurable space, let mu be any finite measure on X, and let f : X -> R be mu-almost everywhere strongly measurable. For every real number M satisfying |f(x)| <= M for mu-almost every x, the two-sided punctured real limit as e tends to 0 of (integral_X klFun(1 + e*f(x)) dmu(x)) / e^2 equals (integral_X f(x)^2 dmu(x)) / 2. Here klFun(t) = t*log(t) + 1 - t, log is the total real logarithm, and the integrals are real Bochner integrals.
objects: An arbitrary measurable space X, a finite measure mu on X, a real-valued function f on X, an almost-everywhere real upper bound M for |f|, the real limiting parameter e, and the real function klFun(t) = t*log(t) + 1 - t.
domains: X is an arbitrary type in an arbitrary universe with a MeasurableSpace structure. mu is a Measure X with IsFiniteMeasure mu. f has domain X and codomain R. M and e are real numbers. log is the total real logarithm, so klFun is a real-valued function on all of R. The approach filter for e is the real neighborhood filter of 0 restricted to R minus {0}. All displayed integrals are real Bochner integrals with respect to mu.
quantifiers: For every X, every measurable-space structure on X, every finite measure mu on X, and every f : X -> R, if f is mu-almost everywhere strongly measurable, then for every real M, if |f(x)| <= M for mu-almost every x, the asserted limit holds. The limit quantifies approach to zero through nonzero real e from either side, with X, mu, f, and M fixed.
assumptions: The only hypotheses are the measurable-space structure on X, finiteness of mu, AEStronglyMeasurable f mu, and, for the chosen real M, |f(x)| <= M for mu-almost every x. No probability normalization of mu, zero-mean condition on f, differentiability hypothesis, pointwise bound at every x, or explicit sign condition on M is assumed. No separate integrability hypothesis is given.
conclusion: Tendsto of e -> (integral_X klFun(1 + e*f(x)) dmu(x)) / e^2 along the two-sided punctured real neighborhood of 0 to the ordinary real neighborhood of (integral_X f(x)^2 dmu(x)) / 2. This asserts convergence of the actual real integral values, with klFun defined by t*log(t) + 1 - t.
scopes: The finite-measure and measurability hypotheses concern the same fixed mu on X. The bound |f(x)| <= M is mu-almost everywhere in x and uses a single M independent of x and e; exceptional representative values of f are permitted. Both integrals range over all x in X with respect to mu. The same f and mu appear on both sides. Only e varies in the limit. The point e = 0 is excluded by the approach filter, regardless of totalized real division. No restriction to positive e, no additional parameter limit, and no probability or density interpretation is part of the statement.
constant_dependencies: M may be any real bound satisfying the almost-everywhere hypothesis for the fixed f and mu; it is fixed during the e limit. The result is universal in X, mu, f, and M. The limiting value depends on f and mu through the integral of f squared and does not contain M. The scalar coefficient 1/2 is universal. No rates, auxiliary constants, or dependence of such constants are asserted.
